title_en: The Passion of Montanus and Lucius
author: Montanus and Lucius (Carthage)
addressee: Christian brethren, addressed as dearest brothers, including future brothers
occasion: After arrest and imprisonment at Carthage, the prisoners write to leave faithful testimony of God's greatness and of their suffering and endurance for the Lord for brothers who will come after.
argument: God protects his servants even in prison: the threatened live burning is extinguished by prayer, prison darkness becomes light, and hunger and thirst are relieved through help brought by fellow Christians. Visions of lamps, a guiding child, milk-filled bowls, white garments, and promises of a more glorious crown assure the prisoners that Christ is with them and that their spirits hasten to God. Therefore they must hold unity, love, peace, and unanimity, since division forfeits sonship and inheritance while agreement obtains whatever is asked. An editor completes the account: after long imprisonment most confessors are condemned and led joyfully to execution, Flavian is separated at sentencing then received back with a fuller account promised later, Lucius goes ahead of the others in the procession because of weakness, and Montanus preaches truth against idols, schism, hasty reconciliation of the lapsed, and disrespect for leaders.

outline.move: Arrest after popular tumult and persecution is listed, then threatened live burning is averted by prayer and the prisoners are sent to dark prison which becomes light.
Renus dreams of lamps going before each prisoner, and after a joyful day the group is dragged before the acting procurator then returned to prison to face hunger and thirst.

Two prison visions promise endurance and relief: Victor the presbyter sees a shining child who says Christ is with them, and Quartillosia reports her martyred son and a huge youth giving unfailing milk and opening the window to heaven.

Expected lack of prison food is relieved when the Lord provides through Lucian, who ministers unfailing food through Herennian the subdeacon and Januarius the catechumen as his instruments like two bowls, strengthening the sick.

The prisoners exhort one another to concord, charity, peace and unanimity as the condition of answered prayer and inheritance, confirmed by Montanus's vision of white garments with a stain of discord with Julian.

An editor adds what modesty omitted: condemnation before the governor with Flavian separated then received back, joyful procession to execution with final encouragements by Lucius, Julian and Victoricus, and Montanus's strong final preaching on idols, schismatics, the lapsed, steadfastness, virgins, and leaders.

cast.name: Montanus
cast.who: Imprisoned confessor and co-author, later executed preaching boldly.

cast.name: Lucius
cast.who: Imprisoned confessor and co-author, weakened by prison, who goes ahead of the others in the procession to execution.

cast.name: Flavian
cast.who: Fellow confessor separated at sentence, then received back, to be told more fully later.

cast.name: Julian
cast.who: Fellow confessor rebuked by Montanus over a woman who crept into their communion but did not communicate, who remained in the cold of discord; the vision shows the stain needing reconciliation.

cast.name: Primolus
cast.who: Arrested Christian whose earlier confession served as baptism.

cast.name: Renus
cast.who: Fellow prisoner who dreams of lamps going before them.

cast.name: Donatian
cast.who: Donatian the catechumen, who when baptized in prison immediately rendered up his spirit, hastening by an immaculate journey from the baptism of water to the crown of martyrdom.

cast.name: Victor
cast.who: Victor the presbyter, fellow martyr who suffered immediately after this same vision.

cast.name: Quartillosia
cast.who: Imprisoned Christian woman whose husband and son were martyred three days earlier.

cast.name: Cyprian
cast.who: Church teacher who taught the faith the martyrs learned.

cast.name: Leucius
cast.who: Figure seen with Cyprian in Montanus's vision.

cast.name: Lucian
cast.who: Dear Christian through whom prison food is provided; in Montanus's account Lucian meets him and hears the vision.

cast.name: Herennian
cast.who: Subdeacon who carries food into prison.

cast.name: Januarius
cast.who: Catechumen who helps carry food into prison.

scripture: conventions: author uses the Old Latin Bible with LXX-style book names and Psalm numbering; quotations are woven in without modern references, including the three youths in the fire, lamp for feet, call on me in distress, two agreeing, peacemakers, sons and heirs, and no sacrifice to other gods; cite in modern form as Daniel 3, Psalm 119:105 (LXX 118:105), Psalm 50:15 (LXX 49:15), Matthew 18:19, Matthew 5:9, Romans 8:16-17, Exodus 22:20, giving LXX Psalm number alongside modern where Psalms occur
uncertain: exact year and governor/procurator names beyond the Valerianic Carthage setting
division of authorship between Montanus, Lucius and companions in sections 1-7
meaning of regionantes and reading cammorum/caminorum for burning furnaces
identity of Leucius seen with Cyprian
identity and kinship details around Quartillosia, her son, husband and Iacobi of the sign, including which James signum Iacobi means
whether fiscalis/solon/solonis denotes a prison ration, tax-official or local term
precise force of negotiatio pacis for the lapsed and full penitential practice implied
whether Lucian meeting Montanus after the vision occurred in waking reality or within the vision narrative

_unresolved_facts.claim: Julian ... fellow confessor rebuked by Montanus over a woman who crept into their communion but did not communicate, who remained in the cold of discord; the vision shows the stain needing reconciliation
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Nam cum Montanus cum Iuliano habuisset sermones aliquos ob eam mulierem quae ad nostram communionem obrepsit, quae non communicabat, cumque post correptionem quam in eum congesserat in frigore ipso discordiae mansisset
_unresolved_facts.fix: Julian: Fellow confessor with whom Montanus had words over a woman who crept into their communion but did not communicate; Montanus had rebuked Julian, but Julian remained in the cold of discord. The vision shows a stain of discord on Montanus's own garment, not Julian's.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Lucian ... in Montanus's account Lucian meets him and hears the vision
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: et occurrit mihi Lucianus, et retuli illi visionem, et aio illi: Scis quia sordes illae illud est quod non statim concordavi cum Iuliano?
_unresolved_facts.source_quote_2: qui statim post hanc eandem visionem passus est
_unresolved_facts.fix: Lucian: Dear Christian through whom prison food is provided; in Montanus's vision account, Lucianus meets him after he wakes and hears the vision retold. (This Lucianus in the vision is likely a different person from the Lucianus of section 5, since the presbyter Victor suffered immediately after the vision, while the food-provider Lucianus ministered over many days.)

_unresolved_facts.claim: Lucian ... in Montanus's account Lucian meets him and hears the vision
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: et occurrit mihi Lucianus, et retuli illi visionem
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Lucianus who meets Montanus after the vision is a figure in the vision narrative or immediately upon waking, not necessarily the same as the food-provider Lucianus of section 5; the text does not clearly identify them as the same person.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Shining boy ... within Victor's vision: puerum introisse with lucid face, who leads and speaks first, marked by ait mihi
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Videbam, inquit, puerum huc in carcerem introisse, cuius fuit vultus perlucidus super splendorem inenarrabilem. qui nos deducebat per omnia loca ut exiremus; egredi tamen non potuimus, et ait mihi: Adhuc modicum laboratis, quia nunc impedimini. sed confidite quia ego vobiscum sum.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Shining boy/child: within Victor's vision, a boy with face more lucid than indescribable splendor enters, leads them through all places to exit, speaks first ('ait mihi'), and adds further words; the figure is then identified as the Lord himself when Victor asks about paradise and the figure responds about faith and gives the sign of Jacob.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Lord ... within Victor's vision distinguished as dominus, who responds further marked by respondit ei dominus et ait, including the words about the sign of Iacobi
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: nam hunc eundem dominum de paradiso interrogavit ubi esset. cui ille ait: Extra mundum est. Ostende mihi illum, inquit. et ait illi: Et ubi erit fides? eumque hoc per humanam pusillitatem diceret: Quod me mandas tenere non possum, dic signum quod eis dicam, respondit ei dominus et ait: Dic illis signum Iacobi.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Lord: The shining boy/child figure is identified as 'dominum' when Victor asks about paradise; the same figure continues speaking, and 'respondit ei dominus et ait' marks the Lord's response about the sign of Jacob. The boy and the Lord are the same figure in the vision, not distinct speakers.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Flavian is separated at sentencing then received back
_unresolved_facts.fix: Flavian is separated at sentencing when his aid reclamaret amore perverso, denying he was a deacon; he is received back into prison (rursum receptus est), not received back for execution with the others.

_unresolved_facts.claim: condemnation before the governor with Flavian separated then received back
_unresolved_facts.fix: condemnation before the governor with Flavian separated at sentencing and received back into prison, with a fuller account of him promised later

_unresolved_facts.claim: Flavian ... Fellow confessor separated at sentence, then received back, to be told more fully later
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Flavianusque rursum receptus est. et quamvis haberet plenam doloris materiam... sed de Flaviano postmodum plenius.
_unresolved_facts.fix: Flavian: Fellow confessor separated at sentence when he denied his diaconate, then received back into prison (not executed with the others), to be told more fully later.
